summary: Admit a provider-neutral connector readiness matrix and catalog-wide Integration Center view without treating manifests or health probes as business qualification.

impacts.evidence: Readiness routes are protected by the resolved tenant scope and the MCP catalog is exposed only after agent identity and permission checks.
Generated matrix contains redacted metadata only; credentials, raw provider responses and PII are excluded.
Read-only connector readiness list/detail operations are additive OpenAPI and generated SDK contracts.
No new event or consumer is introduced; existing outbox/inbox and reconciliation authority remains unchanged.
Readiness profiles reuse the provider-neutral connector capability vocabulary and are exposed through SDK/MCP read surfaces.
The matrix is generated from checked-in redacted evidence; tenant account health and durable sync repositories are reused.
Qualified status fails closed without exact credentialed evidence; no new route accepts secret material.
Readiness is descriptive and cannot bypass existing account, capability, policy or approval gates for writes.
Evidence references and release gate output preserve the reason for each status and next action.
Capability metadata records idempotency/read-after-write expectations while existing durable reconciliation handles unknown outcomes.
No caller-controlled egress or new webhook ingress is added.
Integration Center exposes freshness, blockers, quotas-related evidence and operational next actions.
Runbook documents capability disablement, kill switch, reauthorization and DLQ/reconciliation response.
Matrix generator, static readiness gate, Go tests, OpenAPI parity and frontend build cover the repository boundary.
